title: Relative clauses: adding information about people

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and *quien* from B1 Unit 5. *Que* joins a second piece of information to a noun. With commas it adds extra information about someone you already know (*el Inca, que gobernaba desde Cuzco*); without commas it says which people you mean (*los guerreros que capturaban enemigos*).

items.spanish: El Inca, que gobernaba desde Cuzco, era el jefe del Estado.
items.english: The Inca, who ruled from Cuzco, was the head of the state.

items.spanish: Los guerreros que capturaban enemigos recibían honores.
items.english: The warriors who captured enemies received honours.

items.spanish: Los mexicas tenían un gobernante, el tlatoani, que dirigía la ciudad.
items.english: The Mexica had a ruler, the tlatoani, who led the city.

items.spanish: Los campesinos, que eran la mayoría, pagaban tributo con trabajo.
items.english: The peasants, who were the majority, paid tribute with work.

sections.content: With people, *que* is the normal choice and does not change for gender or number. With commas the sentence is still true if you remove the clause; without commas it is not: not every warrior received honours, only those who captured enemies.
